text_en: January 1, 1925 — Edwin Hubble announced that the Andromeda Nebula is an independent galaxy, far beyond the Milky Way.
January 2, 1492 — The troops of the Catholic Monarchs completed the siege of Granada, ending the last Muslim kingdom on the Iberian Peninsula.
January 3, 1777 — George Washington defeated British troops at the Battle of Princeton during the American Revolutionary War.
January 4, 1643 — Isaac Newton was born, according to the Gregorian calendar, one of the central figures of the scientific revolution.
January 5, 1922 — Explorer Ernest Shackleton died aboard the Quest, off South Georgia, at the start of his final Antarctic expedition.
January 6, 1912 — Alfred Wegener presented his theory of continental drift for the first time.
January 7, 1610 — Galileo Galilei observed the moons of Jupiter for the first time with his telescope.
January 8, 1889 — Herman Hollerith patented a tabulating machine that laid the foundations of data computing.
January 9, 1839 — Louis Daguerre publicly presented the daguerreotype, one of the first photographic processes.
January 10, 1901 — Oil was discovered at Spindletop, Texas, launching the modern American oil boom.
January 11, 1922 — Insulin was administered for the first time to a human patient with diabetes in Toronto.
January 12, 1866 — The Royal Aeronautical Society was founded in London, the world's first aeronautical society.
January 13, 1910 — Engineer Lee de Forest made one of the first public radio broadcasts, airing a live performance from New York's Metropolitan Opera.
January 14, 1943 — The Casablanca Conference between Roosevelt and Churchill began to coordinate Allied military strategy.
January 15, 1967 — The first Super Bowl in history was played, between the Green Bay Packers and the Kansas City Chiefs.
January 16, 1991 — The air campaign of Operation Desert Storm against Iraq began.
January 17, 1912 — Robert Falcon Scott reached the South Pole, a month after the Norwegian expedition led by Amundsen.
January 18, 1778 — Captain James Cook became the first European to sight the Hawaiian Islands.
January 19, 1839 — Charles Darwin was elected a fellow of the Royal Society of London.
January 20, 1892 — The first official basketball game in history was played in Springfield, Massachusetts.
January 21, 1954 — The USS Nautilus, the world's first nuclear-powered submarine, was launched.
January 22, 1879 — The Battle of Rorke's Drift began, one of the most celebrated British military defenses of the Anglo-Zulu War.
January 23, 1849 — Elizabeth Blackwell became the first woman to receive a medical degree in the United States.
January 24, 1986 — NASA's Voyager 2 probe made its closest flyby of Uranus.
January 25, 1915 — Alexander Graham Bell made the first transcontinental telephone call in the United States, between New York and San Francisco.
January 26, 1788 — The British First Fleet arrived in Sydney, founding the first European settlement in Australia.
January 27, 1880 — Thomas Edison patented the long-lasting incandescent lamp.
January 28, 1986 — The Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch.
January 29, 1856 — Queen Victoria instituted the Victoria Cross, the highest British military decoration.
January 30, 1968 — The Tet Offensive began, a series of coordinated attacks by North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces during the Vietnam War.
January 31, 1958 — The United States launched Explorer 1, its first artificial satellite.
February 1, 2003 — The Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart while reentering the atmosphere, killing all seven crew members.
February 2, 1848 — The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed, ending the war between Mexico and the United States.
February 3, 1966 — The Soviet probe Luna 9 achieved the first soft landing on the Moon in history.
February 4, 1938 — Hewlett-Packard was founded; its first product was a precision oscillator used by Disney in the film Fantasia.
February 5, 1971 — Apollo 14 landed in the Fra Mauro region, with Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell aboard.
February 6, 1958 — The aircraft carrying the Manchester United team crashed in Munich, in one of the greatest disasters in football history.
February 7, 1985 — Astronaut Bruce McCandless made the first untethered spacewalk, using a maneuvering unit.
February 8, 1904 — Japan launched a surprise attack on the Russian fleet at Port Arthur, starting the Russo-Japanese War.
February 9, 1895 — William G. Morgan invented volleyball in Massachusetts.
February 10, 1763 — France, Spain, and Great Britain signed the Treaty of Paris, ending the Seven Years' War.
February 11, 2016 — Scientists at the LIGO observatory announced the first direct detection of gravitational waves.
February 12, 1809 — Naturalist Charles Darwin was born in England.
February 13, 1945 — The Allied bombing of Dresden began, one of the most destructive air raids of World War II.
February 14, 1990 — The Voyager 1 probe took the photograph known as the Pale Blue Dot, showing Earth from the edge of the solar system.
February 15, 1898 — The battleship USS Maine exploded in Havana harbor, precipitating the Spanish-American War.
February 16, 1804 — Lieutenant Stephen Decatur led a naval raid to burn the captured frigate USS Philadelphia during the Barbary War.
February 17, 1600 — Astronomer Giordano Bruno was executed in Rome by the Inquisition after defending an infinite universe with multiple suns.
February 18, 1930 — Astronomer Clyde Tombaugh discovered the dwarf planet Pluto.
February 19, 1878 — Thomas Edison patented the phonograph, the first device capable of recording and reproducing sound.
February 20, 1962 — John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth aboard the Friendship 7.
February 21, 1885 — Construction of the Washington Monument was completed, then the tallest structure in the world.
February 22, 1980 — The American ice hockey team defeated the Soviet Union at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics, in the game known as the Miracle on Ice.
February 23, 1945 — U.S. Marines raised the flag on Mount Suribachi during the Battle of Iwo Jima.
February 24, 1582 — Pope Gregory XIII promulgated the Gregorian calendar, now used in most of the world.
February 25, 1836 — Samuel Colt patented the revolver with a rotating cylinder.
February 26, 1616 — Galileo Galilei was formally warned by the Catholic Church to abandon the heliocentric theory.
February 27, 1991 — Ground combat in the Gulf War ended following the liberation of Kuwait.
February 28, 1953 — James Watson and Francis Crick announced the discovery of the double-helix structure of DNA.
February 29, 1504 — Christopher Columbus, stranded in Jamaica, used his knowledge of an upcoming lunar eclipse to persuade the local inhabitants to keep supplying his crew.
March 1, 1954 — The United States detonated the Castle Bravo hydrogen bomb at Bikini Atoll, the largest nuclear test in its history.
March 2, 1949 — The B-50 bomber Lucky Lady II completed the first nonstop flight around the world in aviation history.
March 3, 1918 — Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, withdrawing from World War I.
March 4, 1493 — Christopher Columbus returned to Spain after completing his first voyage to America.
March 5, 1936 — The Spitfire, the British fighter that would prove crucial in the Battle of Britain, flew for the first time.
March 6, 1836 — The Alamo fort in Texas fell after a thirteen-day siege during the Texas Revolution.
March 7, 1876 — Alexander Graham Bell obtained the U.S. patent for the telephone.
March 8, 1945 — American B-29 bombers carried out a massive incendiary raid on Tokyo.
March 9, 1934 — Yuri Gagarin, who would become the first human to travel into space, was born in the USSR.
March 10, 1876 — Alexander Graham Bell made the first successful telephone call in history.
March 11, 2011 — A magnitude 9.0 earthquake and the ensuing tsunami caused the cooling systems of the Fukushima nuclear plant to fail.
March 12, 1938 — German troops entered Austria, formalizing the Anschluss.
March 13, 1781 — William Herschel discovered the planet Uranus.
March 14, 1879 — Physicist Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, Germany.
March 15, 44 — Julius Caesar, Roman general and dictator, was assassinated in the Senate on the Ides of March.
March 16, 1926 — Robert Goddard launched the first liquid-fueled rocket in history.
March 17, 1958 — The United States launched the Vanguard 1 satellite, the oldest artificial satellite still in orbit.
March 18, 1965 — Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov performed the first spacewalk in history.
March 19, 1687 — French explorer René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle was killed by members of his own expedition in Texas.
March 20, 1815 — Napoleon Bonaparte entered Paris at the start of the period known as the Hundred Days.
March 21, 1918 — Germany launched the Spring Offensive on the Western Front, its last major offensive push of World War I.
March 22, 1945 — Allied forces crossed the Rhine River in Operation Plunder, pushing into German territory in the final stretch of World War II.
March 23, 1854 — Inventor Elisha Otis publicly demonstrated the first safety elevator, with an automatic brake in case the cable broke.
March 24, 1989 — The oil tanker Exxon Valdez ran aground in Alaska, causing one of the largest oil spills in history.
March 25, 1655 — Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan, Saturn's largest moon.
March 26, 1953 — Jonas Salk announced the successful development of a vaccine against poliomyelitis.
March 27, 1964 — A magnitude 9.2 earthquake struck Alaska, one of the strongest ever recorded.
March 28, 1979 — A partial nuclear accident occurred at the Three Mile Island plant in Pennsylvania.
March 29, 1974 — Chinese farmers discovered the Terracotta Army in the tomb of the first emperor, Qin Shi Huang.
March 30, 1858 — Hyman Lipman patented the first pencil with an attached eraser.
March 31, 1889 — The Eiffel Tower was inaugurated in Paris for the World's Fair.
April 1, 1976 — Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak founded Apple Computer in a garage in California.
April 2, 1801 — Admiral Horatio Nelson defeated the Danish fleet at the Battle of Copenhagen.
April 3, 1973 — Martin Cooper made the first call from a portable cell phone in New York.
April 4, 1581 — Queen Elizabeth I of England knighted Francis Drake after his circumnavigation of the globe.
April 5, 1722 — Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen sighted Easter Island on Easter Sunday, giving it its name.
April 6, 1909 — Robert Peary claimed to have reached the North Pole together with Matthew Henson.
April 7, 1795 — France officially adopted the decimal metric system.
April 8, 1820 — The statue of the Venus de Milo was discovered on the Greek island of Milos.
April 9, 1865 — Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox, ending the American Civil War.
April 10, 1930 — The Chrysler Building was inaugurated in New York, at the time the tallest skyscraper in the world.
April 11, 1970 — The United States launched the Apollo 13 mission toward the Moon.
April 12, 1961 — Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to travel into space.
April 13, 1970 — An oxygen tank exploded in the Apollo 13 service module, forcing the cancellation of the Moon landing.
April 14, 1912 — The RMS Titanic struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic shortly before midnight.
April 15, 1912 — The RMS Titanic sank in the Atlantic after striking an iceberg, killing more than 1,500 people.
April 16, 1943 — Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann first synthesized lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD).
April 17, 1970 — The Apollo 13 crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean after the in-flight explosion.
April 18, 1906 — A major earthquake struck San Francisco, a key episode in the development of modern seismology.
April 19, 1775 — The battles of Lexington and Concord were fought, the first armed clashes of the American Revolution.
April 20, 1770 — Captain James Cook sighted the east coast of Australia for the first time.
April 21, 1526 — Babur defeated the forces of the Delhi Sultanate at the First Battle of Panipat, using field artillery in India for the first time.
April 22, 1500 — Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral reached the coast of what is now Brazil.
April 23, 1918 — The British Royal Navy launched the Zeebrugge Raid to block the German submarine naval base in Belgium.
April 24, 1990 — The Hubble Space Telescope was launched aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery.
April 25, 1953 — James Watson and Francis Crick published their paper on the structure of DNA in the journal Nature.
April 26, 1937 — The German Condor Legion bombed the Basque town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War.
April 27, 1521 — Explorer Ferdinand Magellan died in the Battle of Mactan, in the Philippines.
April 28, 1789 — The crew of the HMS Bounty mutinied against Captain William Bligh in the South Pacific.
April 29, 1913 — Gideon Sundback patented a modern, functional version of the zipper.
April 30, 1975 — North Vietnamese troops took Saigon, ending the Vietnam War.
May 1, 1931 — The Empire State Building was inaugurated in New York City.
May 2, 1519 — Leonardo da Vinci died in France; his notebooks of anatomical and mechanical studies anticipated scientific and engineering ideas of later centuries.
May 3, 1494 — Christopher Columbus sighted the island of Jamaica for the first time during his second voyage to America.
May 4, 1904 — The United States began construction of the Panama Canal.
May 5, 1961 — Alan Shepard became the first American to travel into space aboard the Freedom 7.
May 6, 1937 — The airship Hindenburg caught fire while landing in New Jersey.
May 7, 1915 — A German submarine sank the ocean liner RMS Lusitania off the coast of Ireland.
May 8, 1945 — Germany signed its unconditional surrender, ending World War II in Europe.
May 9, 1926 — Explorer Richard Byrd claimed to have made the first airplane flight over the North Pole.
May 10, 1869 — The first American transcontinental railroad was completed with the joining of the tracks at Promontory, Utah.
May 11, 1997 — IBM's Deep Blue computer defeated world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a full match.
May 12, 1949 — The Soviet blockade of Berlin ended after nearly eleven months, overcome by the Allied airlift.
May 13, 1940 — Germany began its invasion of France through the Ardennes, bypassing the Maginot Line.
May 14, 1973 — The United States launched the Skylab space station, its first space station.
May 15, 1957 — The United Kingdom detonated its first hydrogen bomb in the Pacific, in Operation Grapple.
May 16, 1943 — RAF squadrons attacked German dams with specially designed bouncing bombs, in the famous Operation Chastise.
May 17, 1875 — The first Kentucky Derby was held in Louisville.
May 18, 1980 — Mount St. Helens erupted in the state of Washington.
May 19, 1935 — Officer T. E. Lawrence, known as Lawrence of Arabia, died in a motorcycle accident in England.
May 20, 1932 — Amelia Earhart took off from Newfoundland to become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
May 21, 1927 — Charles Lindbergh landed in Paris after completing the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight.
May 22, 1906 — The Wright brothers were granted the patent for their flying machine.
May 23, 1430 — Joan of Arc was captured by Burgundian troops at Compiègne during the Hundred Years' War.
May 24, 1844 — Samuel Morse sent the first long-distance telegraph message, between Washington and Baltimore.
May 25, 1961 — President John F. Kennedy announced before Congress the goal of landing a man on the Moon before 1970.
May 26, 1940 — The evacuation of Allied troops from Dunkirk began during World War II.
May 27, 1937 — The Golden Gate Bridge opened to traffic in San Francisco, at the time the longest suspension bridge in the world.
May 28, 1959 — The monkeys Able and Baker returned alive to Earth after a suborbital flight, validating spaceflight for primates.
May 29, 1953 — Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest for the first time.
May 30, 1911 — The first Indianapolis 500 was held.
May 31, 1889 — The failure of the South Fork Dam caused the catastrophic Johnstown Flood in Pennsylvania.
June 1, 1813 — The American frigate Chesapeake was captured by the British Royal Navy off the coast of Boston.
June 2, 1966 — NASA's Surveyor 1 probe achieved the first American soft landing on the Moon.
June 3, 1965 — Edward White performed the first spacewalk by an American astronaut during the Gemini 4 mission.
June 4, 1942 — The Battle of Midway began, a naval turning point in the Pacific during World War II.
June 5, 1967 — Israel launched a preemptive air strike against Egypt, starting the Six-Day War.
June 6, 1944 — Allied forces landed in Normandy in the largest amphibious operation in history.
June 7, 1099 — The Crusader siege of Jerusalem began during the First Crusade.
June 8, 1966 — The merger between the NFL and the AFL was announced, giving rise to modern professional American football.
June 9, 1959 — The USS George Washington, the first submarine armed with nuclear ballistic missiles, was launched.
June 10, 1940 — Italy declared war on France and the United Kingdom, joining World War II.
June 11, 1997 — Michael Jordan scored 38 points despite a severe illness, leading the Chicago Bulls to victory in the famous Flu Game of the NBA Finals.
June 12, 1979 — The human-powered aircraft Gossamer Albatross crossed the English Channel for the first time.
June 13, 1944 — Germany launched its first V1 missile attack against London.
June 14, 1982 — Argentine forces surrendered to the United Kingdom, ending the Falklands War.
June 15, 1752 — Benjamin Franklin carried out his famous kite experiment to study the electrical nature of storms.
June 16, 1963 — Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman to travel into space.
June 17, 1885 — The Statue of Liberty arrived in New York, disassembled into pieces shipped from France for assembly.
June 18, 1815 — The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon Bonaparte at the Battle of Waterloo.
June 19, 1846 — The first baseball game under modern organized rules was played in Hoboken, New Jersey.
June 20, 1948 — Columbia Records introduced the 33 1/3 rpm long-playing record.
June 21, 1948 — The first computer with a stored program in memory, the Manchester Baby, was presented in England.
June 22, 1633 — Galileo Galilei was forced by the Inquisition to recant the heliocentric theory.
June 23, 1868 — Christopher Latham Sholes patented the first practical typewriter.
June 24, 1859 — The Battle of Solferino was fought, whose horrors would inspire the creation of the Red Cross.
June 25, 1876 — Lakota and Cheyenne forces defeated Custer's Seventh Cavalry at the Battle of Little Bighorn.
June 26, 1974 — The first barcode-scanned product was sold at a supermarket in Ohio.
June 27, 1954 — The Obninsk nuclear power plant in the USSR became the world's first nuclear plant to generate electricity for a public grid.
June 28, 1914 — Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria was assassinated in Sarajevo, an event that triggered World War I.
June 29, 2007 — Apple released the first iPhone for sale, transforming the mobile phone industry.
June 30, 1908 — A massive explosion known as the Tunguska event devastated a vast area of Siberia.
July 1, 1863 — The Battle of Gettysburg began, the bloodiest engagement of the American Civil War.
July 2, 1937 — Aviator Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean during her attempt to fly around the world.
July 3, 1886 — Karl Benz publicly presented the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, considered the first automobile.
July 4, 2012 — CERN announced the discovery of the Higgs boson.
July 5, 1687 — Isaac Newton published the Principia Mathematica, the foundational work of classical physics.
July 6, 1885 — Louis Pasteur successfully administered the first rabies vaccine to a human being.
July 7, 1930 — Construction began on the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River, United States.
July 8, 1497 — Vasco da Gama set sail from Lisbon on the expedition that would open the European sea route to India.
July 9, 1893 — Surgeon Daniel Hale Williams performed one of the first successful open-heart surgeries.
July 10, 1940 — The Battle of Britain began, the air campaign between the German Luftwaffe and the British RAF.

July 14, 1965 — The Mariner 4 probe achieved the first successful flyby of Mars, sending back the first close-up images of another planet.
July 15, 1099 — Christian Crusaders conquered Jerusalem after a prolonged siege.
July 16, 1945 — The United States detonated the first atomic bomb in history in the Trinity test, in New Mexico.
July 17, 1975 — Apollo and Soyuz spacecraft docked in orbit, in the first joint space mission between the United States and the USSR.
July 18, 1968 — Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore founded Intel, a company key to the development of modern semiconductors.
July 19, 1545 — The English warship Mary Rose sank in the Solent strait.
July 20, 1969 — Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon.
July 21, 1861 — The First Battle of Bull Run was fought, the first major land engagement of the American Civil War.
July 22, 1298 — King Edward I of England defeated William Wallace's Scots at the Battle of Falkirk.
July 23, 1885 — General Ulysses S. Grant, commander of Union forces during the American Civil War, died.
July 24, 1911 — Explorer Hiram Bingham rediscovered the Inca ruins of Machu Picchu in Peru.
July 25, 1978 — Louise Brown, the first person conceived through in vitro fertilization, was born in England.
July 26, 1945 — The Allies issued the Potsdam Declaration, demanding Japan's unconditional surrender.
July 27, 1953 — The armistice ending the fighting in the Korean War was signed.
July 28, 1914 — Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia, formally starting World War I.
July 29, 1958 — The U.S. Congress created NASA, the country's civilian space agency.
July 30, 1932 — The 1932 Summer Olympics opened in Los Angeles.
July 31, 1971 — Apollo 15 astronauts drove a lunar rover on the Moon's surface for the first time.
August 1, 1774 — Chemist Joseph Priestley first isolated oxygen as a gas.
August 2, 1990 — Iraq invaded Kuwait, triggering the crisis that would lead to the Gulf War.
August 3, 1492 — Christopher Columbus set sail from the port of Palos bound for what would become the American continent.
August 4, 1914 — The United Kingdom declared war on Germany following the invasion of Belgium, entering World War I.
August 5, 1930 — Astronaut Neil Armstrong, who years later would walk on the Moon, was born in Ohio.
August 6, 1945 — The United States dropped the first atomic bomb used in combat on the city of Hiroshima.

August 19, 1909 — The first race was held at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway.
August 20, 1977 — NASA launched the Voyager 2 probe toward the outer planets of the solar system.

August 22, 1485 — Richard III of England died at the Battle of Bosworth, ending the Plantagenet dynasty.

August 26, 1940 — The British Royal Air Force bombed Berlin for the first time during World War II.

August 30, 1983 — Guion Bluford became the first African American to travel into space, aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger.
August 31, 1897 — Thomas Edison patented the Kinetograph, one of the first motion picture cameras.
September 1, 1939 — Germany invaded Poland, an event that started World War II.
September 2, 1945 — Japan signed its formal surrender aboard the USS Missouri, ending World War II.
September 3, 1783 — The Treaty of Paris was signed, ending the American War of Independence.

October 1, 1908 — Ford began mass production of the Model T automobile.
October 2, 1187 — Sultan Saladin conquered Jerusalem after defeating the Crusaders.

November 20, 1945 — The Nuremberg trials of top Nazi leaders for war crimes began.
November 21, 1783 — The first crewed hot air balloon flight in history took place in Paris.
November 22, 1943 — Roosevelt, Churchill, and Chiang Kai-shek met at the Cairo Conference to coordinate Allied strategy against Japan.
November 23, 1876 — The first documented soccer match in Argentina was played in Buenos Aires.
November 24, 1859 — Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species.
November 25, 1867 — Alfred Nobel patented dynamite.
November 26, 1965 — France launched Astérix, its first artificial satellite, becoming the world's third space power.
November 27, 1942 — The French fleet scuttled itself at Toulon to keep it from falling into German hands.
November 28, 1520 — Ferdinand Magellan reached the Pacific Ocean after crossing the strait that now bears his name.
November 29, 1929 — Admiral Richard Byrd made the first airplane flight over the South Pole.
November 30, 1954 — A meteorite struck a house in Sylacauga, Alabama, injuring a woman, one of the few documented cases of a person being hit by a meteorite.
December 1, 1990 — The connection between the French and British tunnel boring machines under the English Channel was completed for the Channel Tunnel.
December 2, 1942 — Enrico Fermi achieved the first self-sustaining, controlled nuclear chain reaction in history, in Chicago.
December 3, 1967 — Surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant in South Africa.
December 4, 1965 — NASA launched the Gemini 7 mission, which set a duration record for crewed spaceflight.
December 5, 1492 — Christopher Columbus landed on the island of Hispaniola during his first voyage.
December 6, 1917 — An explosion aboard a munitions ship devastated the port of Halifax, Canada, one of the largest accidental explosions before the nuclear age.
December 7, 1941 — Japan attacked the American naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
December 8, 1941 — The United States declared war on Japan following the attack on Pearl Harbor.
December 9, 1968 — Engineer Douglas Engelbart publicly demonstrated the computer mouse, hypertext, and videoconferencing for the first time, in the famous Mother of All Demos.
December 10, 1901 — The Nobel Prizes were awarded for the first time, in Stockholm.
December 11, 1972 — Apollo 17 astronauts landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley, in the most recent crewed mission to the Moon to date.
December 12, 1901 — Guglielmo Marconi received the first transatlantic radio signal in history.
December 13, 1577 — Francis Drake set sail from England on the voyage that would make him the first Englishman to circumnavigate the globe.
December 14, 1911 — Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen became the first human to reach the South Pole.
December 15, 1965 — The Gemini 6 and Gemini 7 spacecraft achieved the first crewed orbital rendezvous in spaceflight history.
December 16, 1944 — Germany launched its last major offensive on the Western Front, the Battle of the Bulge.
December 17, 1903 — The Wright brothers made the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered airplane at Kitty Hawk.
December 18, 1912 — The discovery of the Piltdown Man skull was announced in England, later revealed to be one of the most famous scientific frauds in history.
December 19, 1777 — George Washington's Continental Army settled into Valley Forge to endure the harsh winter.
December 20, 1951 — The EBR-I experimental reactor in Idaho became the first nuclear reactor to generate usable electricity.
December 21, 1620 — The Mayflower Pilgrims landed at Plymouth, on the coast of Massachusetts.
December 22, 1944 — American troops rejected a German surrender ultimatum during the siege of Bastogne.
December 23, 1947 — The transistor was demonstrated for the first time at Bell Labs.
December 24, 1968 — The Apollo 8 crew became the first to orbit the Moon.
December 25, 1758 — Halley's Comet reappeared exactly as astronomer Edmond Halley had predicted, posthumously confirming his calculation of the comet's orbit.
December 26, 1898 — Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of the element radium.
December 27, 1831 — Charles Darwin set sail from England aboard the HMS Beagle on his scientific voyage of exploration.
December 28, 1895 — The Lumière brothers held the first public film screening with their camera-projector, the Cinématographe.
December 29, 1972 — Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crashed in the Everglades, an accident that led to key reforms in aviation cabin safety procedures.
December 30, 1903 — A fire at the Iroquois Theatre in Chicago led to key reforms in fire safety codes for public buildings.
December 31, 1968 — The Soviet Tupolev Tu-144 became the first supersonic passenger aircraft to fly, beating the Concorde by weeks.
